completeness.repository_coverage: linprog highs path (_linprog.py, _linprog_util.py, _linprog_highs.py, _highspy/_highs_wrapper.py) and sparse kron/hstack/vstack construction; HiGHS C++ core not examined

unknowns.subject: Whether the pybind11 binding returns a copy of col_status/col_dual on each attribute access
unknowns.what_would_resolve_it: Inspect the _core binding source or profile with cProfile/py-spy

unknowns.subject: Time spent inside highs.run() versus the Python marginals loop

known: Workload calls linprog(method='highs') with n=500, d=5, 3 requested quantiles and coherence_buffer=3 (workload.py)
unknown: Binding copy semantics of basis.col_status / solution.col_dual
assumed: Binding properties return a fresh Python list/array per access (typical for pybind11 def_readwrite on std::vector)
derived: num_quantiles = (3-1)*(1+3)+1 = 9; numcol = 9*5*2 + 9*500*2 = 9090 columns, so the loop runs 9090 iterations

root_causes.description: Per-element Python loop over solver columns that re-fetches whole result vectors from the native HiGHS object on each iteration (quadratic).

findings.problem: The bound-marginal computation loops in Python over every column and indexes basis.col_status[ii] and solution.col_dual[ii] on the native objects each iteration. If each attribute access materializes the whole vector, the loop is O(numcol^2) on top of the solve.
findings.performance_principle: Do not cross a language/serialization boundary per element; fetch bulk data once and operate on it vectorized.

evidence.statement: for ii in range(numcol): reads basis.col_status[ii] (up to twice) and solution.col_dual[ii] inside the loop; the basis and solution objects are native HiGHS objects.
Workload sizes: 9 extended quantiles; numcol = 9*5 (beta) + 9*5 (t) + 2*9*500 (deltas) = 9090, derived from workload.py parameters and the construction in coherent_linear_quantile_regression.
The result marg_bnds is only needed for the lower/upper marginals and is built unconditionally for every LP solve, whether or not the caller reads res.lower.marginals.
No runtime evidence supplied; binding copy semantics not inspected.

findings.conditions: Every linprog(method='highs*') call; cost grows with number of columns. In the workload (9090 columns, mostly sparse constraint LP) the loop count is large relative to the solver itself. Quadratic only if the binding copies the vector per access; otherwise linear with a large Python constant.

counter_evidence.statement: Binding source (_core) not available/inspected, so per-access copy is assumed rather than verified.
HiGHS solve itself (highs.run) on a ~13k-row, ~9k-col LP may dominate; cannot be separated statically.

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: If the pybind property returns a cheap view or the solve dominates runtime, the loop is a small share. Small LPs (tens of columns) are unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Fetch basis.col_status and solution.col_dual once, convert to numpy arrays, and compute marg_bnds with boolean masks (lower = status == kLower; upper = status == kUpper). Optionally compute lazily only when marginals are requested.

alternatives.option: Hoist col_status = basis.col_status and col_dual = solution.col_dual before the loop but keep the loop
alternatives.why: Removes the quadratic term but leaves a 9090-iteration Python loop.

alternatives.option: Vectorize with numpy masks after a single fetch
alternatives.why: Removes both the repeated fetch and the per-element interpreter overhead.

findings.trade_offs: Minimal; a small allocation for two arrays of length numcol. Must preserve exact semantics for statuses other than kLower/kUpper (left at zero).

validation.metric: Wall time of _highs_wrapper outside highs.run() for the workload LP
validation.expectation: The Python marginals section drops from O(numcol^2) or O(numcol) interpreted steps to a few array operations; total time falls by the share the loop currently takes.
validation.falsifier: A profile showing the loop is negligible versus highs.run(), or identical timing with the vectors hoisted.

commands.purpose: Show time in _highs_wrapper loop versus highs.run (run from a scratch environment, not the repo tree)

considered_not_reported.observation: linprog bounds given as a 9090-element list of tuples is converted via np.array_equal(bounds, []) and np.array(bounds, dtype=float) in _clean_inputs
considered_not_reported.why_discarded: Linear, vectorized C-level conversion of ~9k tuples; small constant relative to the problem.

considered_not_reported.observation: Sparse construction (kron, hstack, vstack via COO) and csc conversion
considered_not_reported.why_discarded: All implemented with vectorized numpy; linear in nnz; no per-element Python loops.
